name: Johannes Fahrenfort
bio: I am a cognitive neuroscientist in the Cognitive Psychology department at VU Amsterdam and the Brain and Cognition group at UvA. In the Conscious Brain Lab we use EEG, fMRI and psychophysics to investigate consciousness, perceptual bias, confidence, and automatic sensory control. I developed the open-source ADAM toolbox for multivariate EEG/MEG decoding.

name: Simon van Gaal
bio: I am a cognitive neuroscientist working at the Brain and Cognition group (Department of Psychology) of the University of Amsterdam. In our lab we study the neural correlates of consciousness and the role of consciousness in cognitive control and decision-making using various neuroimaging techniques (e.g., high-density EEG, functional and structural MRI, MEG).

name: Timo Stein
bio: Before joining the Brain and Cognition group at UvA, I was an assistant professor at the University of Trento and a postdoctoral fellow at the Max Planck Institute in Frankfurt. My research focuses on visual awareness, face and object recognition, and the dynamics of unconscious processing.

name: Ivan Ivanchei
bio: I joined the Conscious Brain Lab in August 2024 with a Marie Curie project on probabilistic learning and awareness. My research investigates how people become aware of what they learn in probabilistic environments, using behavioral, metacognitive, and physiological indices.

name: Maartje de Jong

name: Ana-Maria Barosan
bio: I started my PhD at the Conscious Brain Lab in September 2024, supervised by Simon van Gaal. My research investigates how consciousness unfolds in time and space using advanced EEG and behavioral paradigms.
